Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

blockr.script 0.0.0.9000

  • new_script_block(): a block whose state is an R script. A top-level assignment of a plain value becomes a control on the block, and the exported code is the script with the current values written in. The editor’s “Start from” menu offers starter scripts.
  • new_prose_block(): markdown with inline R, as ‘Quarto’ writes it.
  • html_page(): a script result that draws as a sandboxed frame, either from a mustache template filled from the input or from a URL.
  • Both blocks take any number of inputs. The first one reads as data.
  • block_result_output(): a generic another package can extend to draw its own result class.
  • block_result_update(): a generic for a result class that can change what it has on screen. The block calls it when the result drawn last is still on screen and the new one has the same class, and then leaves its output as it is, so a scroll position or a search text survives a change of a control.
  • new_script_block() takes class and starters, so another package can build a block of its own on the script block, with its own list under “Start from”. A saved board restores such a block through its own constructor.
  • result_head(): a block_result_output() method puts tools into the block’s head row, left of the gear, and gives the sentence titles for the lines the script does not declare.
  • result_titles(): the title, subtitle and caption now on screen, as text, for a download or a caption drawn under a table. declared and templates say which lines the script wrote and how, and ui = FALSE leaves out the script’s ui_* lines.
  • sentence_data(): a generic for the data frame the sentence’s data tokens read. A dm input now gives {label(col)} its column labels.
  • script_expr(): a script as one expression with the control values written in, for a place that has no block, such as a report.
  • While a script runs for longer than about 300 ms, the result dims and a line above it counts the wait (“computing… 1.2 s”), as blockr.viz’s outputs do.
  • A result no longer goes pale and comes back when its dock tab is shown again. Shiny’s fade of a recalculating output is off on the result; the busy cue above is what shows an evaluation.
  • A NULL written in a script is kept: x <- NULL no longer fails with “incorrect number of arguments”, and function(a = NULL) NULL keeps its formal and its body.
  • On a dock card the rule between the head row and the result is gone while the script tray is closed.
  • A list word of the sentence whose menu is open follows the word when R draws it again: the open list takes the new choices and drops a pick that is no longer among them.
  • The select controls need a ‘blockr.ui’ whose Blockr.Select has list(), where a multi-select shows its picks as text and in the list. An older build is reported on the page and in the browser console.

Developed by Christoph Sax, Nicolas Bennett, Bristol Myers Squibb.
